headline: iPhone Duo's hinge hides a clever cooling trick, sources suggest
summary: Apple's thermal engineers have reportedly found an innovative way to use the hinge of their upcoming foldable iPhone to enhance its cooling capabilities, addressing a key challenge for folding devices.
details: Apple's thermal engineering team has reportedly devised an innovative solution for cooling its upcoming foldable iPhone, utilizing the device's hinge. This approach aims to address the unique thermal challenges posed by folding form factors.

The design is said to leverage the hinge mechanism to actively contribute to heat dissipation, a critical factor for maintaining performance in compact, high-power devices. This creative use of existing components highlights Apple's potential focus on integrated design.

headline_marked: [[Intel's GPU D-Series AI accelerator]] delivers 1.3 PFLOPS FP8 and 1.5 TB/s memory bandwidth
headline: Intel's GPU D-Series AI accelerator delivers 1.3 PFLOPS FP8 and 1.5 TB/s memory bandwidth
summary: The new AI inference accelerators, formerly 'Crescent Island', feature up to 480GB LPDDR5X memory and are designed for air-cooled PCIe systems, targeting large language models and multi-tenant AI services.
details: At OCP 2026, Intel officially named its Crescent Island chip the Intel GPU D-Series. It revealed a theoretical peak performance of 1.3 PFLOPS of FP8 and a memory bandwidth of 1.5 TB/s for these new AI inference accelerators.
The GPU D-Series is built on Intel's Xe3P architecture and will be released in an air-cooled PCIe form factor. These chips have a 350W TDP and support up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory.
Unlike Nvidia's liquid-cooled Rubin GPUs, the D-Series targets a different performance envelope and infrastructure. It's designed for traditional air-cooled rack servers, scaling up to eight GPUs.
Intel states D-Series chips can power inference for models exceeding one trillion parameters. They are suitable for large language models and long-context inference.
The accelerators also support concurrent inference services, creating a foundation for multi-tenant AI services, robotics, and other latency-sensitive workloads.

For distributed inference deployments, a robust software stack is crucial. Intel highlights its common Xe software foundation, already built for AI across its Xe Cores in iGPUs and discrete GPU products.
Intel is collaborating with a broad ecosystem of OEMs, ODMs, neoclouds, and ISVs to bring Xe accelerators to data centers. Customer sampling of GPU D-Series products is currently in progress.
The D-Series aims to give Intel a stronger foothold in the AI accelerator market after previous challenges. Its accessible thermal and electrical envelope could be key to gaining traction.
caption:
Intel's new GPU D-Series AI accelerator is here, boasting 1.3 PFLOPS of FP8 performance and 1.5 TB/s memory bandwidth.

At OCP 2026, Intel officially named its Crescent Island chip the Intel GPU D-Series. It revealed a theoretical peak performance of 1.3 PFLOPS of FP8 and a memory bandwidth of 1.5 TB/s for these new AI inference accelerators.

The GPU D-Series is built on Intel's Xe3P architecture and will be released in an air-cooled PCIe form factor. These chips have a 350W TDP and support up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory.

Unlike Nvidia's liquid-cooled Rubin GPUs, the D-Series targets a different performance envelope and infrastructure. It's designed for traditional air-cooled rack servers, scaling up to eight GPUs.

Intel states D-Series chips can power inference for models exceeding one trillion parameters. They are suitable for large language models and long-context inference.

The accelerators also support concurrent inference services, creating a foundation for multi-tenant AI services, robotics, and other latency-sensitive workloads.

For distributed inference deployments, a robust software stack is crucial. Intel highlights its common Xe software foundation, already built for AI across its Xe Cores in iGPUs and discrete GPU products.

Intel is collaborating with a broad ecosystem of OEMs, ODMs, neoclouds, and ISVs to bring Xe accelerators to data centers. Customer sampling of GPU D-Series products is currently in progress.

The D-Series aims to give Intel a stronger foothold in the AI accelerator market after previous challenges. Its accessible thermal and electrical envelope could be key to gaining traction.
